title: Borland Turbo Basic
summary: A historical overview of Borland Turbo Basic, a popular BASIC compiler and IDE released by Borland in 1987 for DOS systems, competing directly with Microsoft's QuickBASIC and making programming accessible to hobbyist developers during the DOS era.
problem_solved: Provided hobbyist programmers with an affordable, integrated development environment for creating DOS applications in BASIC.
why_valuable: Preserves computing history by documenting an influential programming tool that shaped many developers' early coding experiences in the 1980s-90s.
